::: {.learner-hero}
Learner hub for University of Utah Internal Medicine residents preparing to lead Code Blue and Rapid Response teams while working with bedside nurses, nurse-led response teams, and critical care outreach teams. Use this site before, during, and after the in-person session to orient to the micro-skills, scenarios, and resources.
:::

## Start Here

::: {.hub-grid}
::: {.hub-card}
### Before the Session

- No required module review beforehand; we will spend the first 10 minutes walking through the micro-skill modules together.
- Bring questions from real code/RRT experiences, especially moments when resident and nursing roles felt unclear.
- Complete the pre-session survey when the 2026 link is released.

**Survey status:** 2026 link TBD.
:::

::: {.hub-card}
### During the Session

- Practice taking explicit leadership.
- Interpret shockable and non-shockable rhythms out loud.
- Practice a 30-second huddle with the bedside or outreach nurse.
- Escalate resources early when the room is not safe enough.
- Run hands-on Zoll and scenario practice.
:::

::: {.hub-card}
### After the Session

- Bookmark the resources page.
- Revisit the case rhythm strips.
- Send near-misses, big wins, or unclear resident/nursing workflows to the CMRs or course leads so this course stays current.

**Post-session survey:** 2026 link TBD.
:::
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of the session, learners should be able to:

- Assume and communicate team leadership immediately on arrival.
- Identify VF/VT on the monitor and deliver shocks when warranted.
- Integrate bedside nurse, nurse-led rapid response, or critical care outreach input into the first assessment and plan.
- Escalate care and marshal resources appropriately across U of U, IMED, and VA workflows.
- Conclude the event, hand off ownership, and set up a brief debrief.

::: {.callout-tip}
Didactics alone have limits. Regular review, simulation, interprofessional practice, and feedback after real events are what turn these skills into reflexes.
:::

## Why This Course Exists

Code Blue and Rapid Response leadership is not just algorithm recall. The resident leader has to make the room work: claim the leader role, make roles visible, keep communication psychologically safe, integrate bedside expertise, and escalate resources before the response stalls.

Stakeholders from Code Blue and Rapid Response teams, including senior residents, nurses, respiratory therapists, and quality leads, identified four recurring hazards during resident-led responses:

1. Unclear team leadership, which can cause role confusion, low psychological safety, and decreased collaboration. [@steinbach_effective_2024]
2. Failure to cardiovert or defibrillate shockable rhythms.
3. Delayed critical decisions, including calling for help, initial stabilization, and transport to ICU.
4. Poorly defined collaboration between residents and bedside nurses, nurse-led rapid response teams, or critical care outreach teams.

This seminar targets those hazards through brief micro-skills, discussion, hands-on scenarios, and interprofessional scripts that can be used during real events.
